newsitem.title: UK: Sellers back off at close of Euro veg oil market.
newsitem.headline: Sellers back off at close of Euro veg oil market.

text.p: Sellers trimmed their prices towards the close of the European vegetable oil market on Monday following the sharply lower opening in Chicago.
Chicago soy futures fell sharply on reports of rain in the Midwest and forecasts calling for further falls during the early part of the week.
However, traders in Europe were awaiting events over the next few day's before committing themselves.
They said the Midwest needs a good soaking and the next 48 hours would hold the key to the market for the next week or so.

"Chicago is falling on the reports and forecasts of rain, but most people are waiting to see what happens because if there is not enough rain the market is expected to rally around midweek," said one trader.
The firm dollar will also have its part to play, limiting any downside movement in Europe.

Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong's latest crop report had little impact. Wong forecast an increase of five percent in local palm oil output during July while stocks were projected at 865,000 to 875,000 tonnes at end-July against PORLA's end-June figure of 786,123.
Data released after the Malaysian futures market closed by cargo surveyor SGS put exports n the July 1-20 period at 444,956 tonnes against 369,494 during June 1-20.
Traders said an increase in exports would normally be expected to trigger a rally, even if short-lived, on the Malaysian market, but a lot depended on how Chicago performs.
At the close Dutch soy oil was 0.50 to one guilder down while rape oil was 0.50 to 0.75 guilders lower in tradeless markets.
Crude palm oil closed $7.50 to $10 lower while products were mixed with RBD palm oil unchanged to $2.50 up and olein $2.50 to $5 down.
Coconut oil closed unchanged while palmkernel oil was $2.50 to $5 higher in neglected markets.
